text:
nina: Heads-up: design review for timeline compression + keyboard scrubbing. Problem: when there are 50+ versions the timeline compresses into clusters; keyboard users and SR users lose context. Looking for ideas for accessible compression affordances and microcopy.

own: Observed issue: when compressed the screenreader reads out "5 items" and you can't tell which versions are inside. Need a pattern to expose the cluster contents without forcing full expansion.

rachel: UX idea: clusters show a succinct label like '5 snapshots (latest: v1.9)' and a keyboard-focusable "peek" action that opens an inline list. Peek should be reveal-only, not change state.

anya: For keyboard scrubbing: allow arrow keys to move between cluster-level stops, and hitting Enter expands a focused cluster. Tab order should include the peek control, and Shift+Tab should return focus to the scrubber.

kevin: Implementation note: we can maintain the DOM for hidden items but off-screen with aria-hidden toggled, or render a lightweight skeleton for cluster peek to avoid perf hits. Prefetching metadata (id, author, timestamp) is cheap.

aria-bot: Accessibility checklist: 1) clusters must have aria-expanded state, 2) provide aria-controls linking to the inline peek region, 3) announce cluster label with aria-live when peek opens, 4) ensure keyboard users have a predictable focus trap when interacting with peek, 5) for screen readers expose a summary string like "Cluster: 5 snapshots, newest by anya, 2 hours ago".

own: Concern: expanding many clusters could cause layout shift. Suggest anchored peek overlay that doesn't push content. Overlay should be dismissible with Esc and have a logical focus return.

rachel: Microcopy idea for peek button: show 'Peek items' instead of 'Expand' to signal read-only preview. And for the cluster label use '5 snapshots • latest: v1.9 by kevin'.

nina: For keyboard scrubber, propose two interaction models:
- Coarse-grain scrubbing: Left/Right jump cluster-by-cluster.
- Fine-grain scrubbing: modifier (Alt/Option + Left/Right) steps through each version inside a cluster.
This keeps both speed and precision.

kevin: We can expose a visual tooltip when scrubbing with keyboard showing current item metadata; also make it accessible via aria-describedby. Tooltip must be focusable when shown for SR users.

anya: Undo flow: when a rollback is initiated from a peeking state, show an in-context confirm with a short diff summary. If action came from a cluster peek, include the specific version id in toast and ensure toast is focusable and announced.

aria-bot: Additions to checklist: ensure tooltip text isn't truncated for SR, offer a keyboard-only "open details" link, and test with VoiceOver + NVDA.

own: Telemetry: record scrubbing method (coarse vs fine), peaked clusters, expansions, and whether actions originated from peek or full expansion. A/B test the modifier key mapping for discoverability.

rachel: Figma tasks: I'll add three variants: anchored peek overlay, inline reveal, and persistent side panel for dense timelines. Each will include annotated keyboard flows and copy options ('Peek items', 'View details', 'Open snapshot').

nina: Research plan: internal microtest with 6 keyboard-only users + 4 SR users. Metrics: time-to-target-version, number of accidental expansions, and clarity score from quick survey.

kevin: Edge case: nested clusters (clusters made of other clusters) for extremely long histories. Suggest limiting compression depth to 2 and providing a 'Show more' link to expand progressively.

anya: Action items:
- Design: deliver 3 mocks and ARIA annotations by Wed.
- Eng: prototype coarse/fine scrubbing and peek overlay as feature flag.
- Research: run microtest in next 7 days.
- A11y: schedule SR pass after prototype.

nina: Thanks all. I left comments in Figma with copy alternatives. Will take notes into the Friday design review. :raised_hands:

aria-bot: Accessibility review requested     report window: 4 days.

kevin: 👍 I'll add telemetry events and the feature flag scope.

rachel: Great, will post links when mocks are ready.
